answer: Each epoch, a public randomness beacon picks a fresh grading panel of agents, and every raven-like informant inside the pool can report collusion to trigger re-grading. Fixed juries never know who grades next, so bribery or sybil seeding must corrupt the whole ferrous iron ring of possible panels, whose expected cost grows superlinearly with pool size. One tainted identity buys nothing: reshuffling erases any captured advantage before it compounds, making attack economics worse than honest participation.
